label: Executive Summary
text: The Anomaly Upload Validator is a browser-based internal tool that automates the pre-upload preparation of inspection datasets for Platform A. It accepts raw Input Source exports in CSV or XLSX format, validates them against the Platform A upload specification, converts field values across three nomenclature systems (Input Source → Platform A → Platform B), enables human-in-the-loop resolution of unmatched values, and produces a formatted multi-tab XLSX working document ready for upload. The tool is distributed as a single self-contained HTML file requiring no installation, no server, and no authentication. All data processing runs client-side — no inspection data is transmitted externally.

label: Problem Statement
text: Background Platform B wind farm asset owners engage both Platform A and third-party inspector Input Source for blade inspections. When third-party-sourced data needs to be ingested into Platform A and submitted to Platform B, it must pass through two conversion layers and conform to the Platform A upload specification. Problems Identified Manual pre-upload checking was performed in spreadsheets with no standardized process, leading to inconsistent results and occasional failed uploads. Field value conversion across three nomenclature systems was performed manually using a reference spreadsheet, requiring significant coordinator time per dataset. Unrecognized field values had no structured resolution workflow — they were either missed or required escalation to Engineering via email. Multiple Input Source export formats exist across different client datasets, causing conversion failures when the wrong template was applied. Impact: Each failed upload or conversion error requires manual rework estimated at 30–90 minutes per dataset.

label: Users & Personas
text: Data Coordinator (Primary User) Receives raw Input Source exports from clients and prepares them for upload to Platform A. Non-technical. Needs clear pass/fail feedback without reading code or formulas. Engineering / Data Lead (Secondary User) Owns the conversion mapping tables and is responsible for extending them when new damage types or component combinations appear. Comfortable with spreadsheets. Needs to update the Conversions tab without breaking the output. Operations Manager (Stakeholder) Needs confidence that data being uploaded to Platform A and onward to Platform B is accurate and complete. Reviews compliance scores and flags for escalation.

label: Assumptions & Constraints
text: Assumptions All source files are Input Source exports. Tool is not designed for other inspection platform formats. The first sheet of any XLSX file contains the inspection data. Column names are consistent within a given client's export format. Engineering is responsible for maintaining and extending the Conversions tab. Platform A upload specification does not change between tool versions without a corresponding tool update. Constraints No server infrastructure available — tool must run entirely client-side. Google Apps Script deployment is restricted by company IT policy for user-facing web apps. Distribution via shared Google Drive is the approved method. SheetJS is the only permitted third-party dependency. VLOOKUP row ranges in exported XLSX are calculated at export time. Engineering adding rows beyond the current range requires manual formula updates.

label: US-01 — Upload a dataset file
text: US-01 — Upload a dataset file EP-01 — File Ingestion Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want to upload a CSV or XLSX file by dragging it into the tool or browsing for it, so that I can begin validating a dataset without needing any technical setup. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Tool accepts .csv, .xlsx, and .xls file formats. AC-02: User can drag and drop a file onto the designated drop zone. AC-03: User can alternatively click the drop zone to open a file browser. AC-04: On successful load, the filename and total data row count are displayed. AC-05: If the file is empty or cannot be parsed, a clear error message is shown and no validation runs. AC-06: No file data is transmitted to any external server at any point.

label: US-02 — Have column names normalized automatically
text: US-02 — Have column names normalized automatically EP-01 — File Ingestion Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to automatically handle common column name variations in source platform exports, so that I don't have to manually rename columns before uploading. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: "Date" is treated as "Inspection Date". AC-02: "Blade Chamber" is treated as "BladeChamber". AC-03: "Chord (%)" is treated as "Chord(%)". AC-04: "Turbine Serial Number" is treated as "Serial Number". AC-05: "Links" is treated as "Source Images". AC-06: Unrecognized column names are passed through unchanged and do not cause errors. AC-07: Normalisation is applied silently — no notification shown to the user. Note: Alias map is defined as a named constant in the tool script. Engineering can extend it without touching validation logic.

label: US-25 — Upload a file that has a metadata preamble above the header row
text: US-25 — Upload a file that has a metadata preamble above the header row EP-01 — File Ingestion Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.3 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want a file whose header row sits below several rows of metadata to be read correctly, so that I do not have to delete rows by hand before uploading. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: The header row is located automatically within the first 25 rows of the sheet. AC-02: The row scoring the most recognised column names is chosen as the header. AC-03: Rows above the detected header are ignored and do not become data rows. AC-04: The detected header row number is reported back on the upload confirmation. AC-05: A file whose header is on row 1 is unaffected. Note: Before v2.3 the tool assumed row 1 was the header, so any export carrying a preamble failed at ingestion.

label: US-03 — See which required columns are missing
text: US-03 — See which required columns are missing EP-02 — Validation Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to tell me which required columns are missing from my dataset, so that I can fix the file before attempting an upload. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Tool checks for all 18 required column headers after alias normalisation. AC-02: Missing required columns are displayed as individual cards showing field name and description. AC-03: Missing conditional columns (Serial Number, BladeChamber, Chord(%), Recommendation) are shown as informational — they do not block the export. AC-04: Column name matching is case-sensitive. AC-05: Missing column cards appear before the row-level issues table.

label: US-04 — See which rows have field errors
text: US-04 — See which rows have field errors EP-02 — Validation Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want to see exactly which rows have missing or incorrectly formatted required fields, so that I know what needs to be fixed before the dataset can be uploaded. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Every data row is validated against all required field rules after normalisation and conversion. AC-02: Each issue is shown with: Row number, Anomaly ID, Field name, Status badge, and detail message. AC-03: Severity must be an integer between 1 and 5 inclusive. AC-04: Critical must be "Yes" or "No" (case-insensitive). AC-05: Inspection Date must match YYYY-MM-DD format exactly. AC-06: "Damage Location" must be "Internal" or "External" (case-insensitive). AC-07: Distance (m), Length (m), Width (m) must be numeric values. AC-08: Coordinates must contain at least three [x,y] bracketed pairs. AC-09: Empty required fields raise an Error, except for Asset and Coordinates (see US-06).

label: US-05 — Validate Blade Side using full descriptive names
text: US-05 — Validate Blade Side using full descriptive names EP-02 — Validation Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.2 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to accept both abbreviated codes and full descriptive names for Blade Side values, so that datasets using either naming convention pass validation without manual editing. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: "Code 1" and "Value 1" are both accepted. AC-02: "Code 2" and "Value 2" are both accepted. AC-03: "Code 3" and "Value 3" are both accepted. AC-04: "Code 4" and "Value 4" are both accepted. AC-05: Matching is case-insensitive. AC-06: Any value not in the above list raises an Error. Note: Expanded in v1.2. Original v1.0 accepted two-character codes only.

label: US-06 — See conditional field warnings separately from hard errors
text: US-06 — See conditional field warnings separately from hard errors EP-02 — Validation Field Detail Persona Engineering / Data Lead Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.2 User Story: As a Engineering / Data Lead, I want conditional field format issues to appear as Warnings rather than Errors, so that they don't inflate the error count or block the export. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Conditional fields are validated for format only when present and populated. AC-02: Format violations in conditional fields raise a Warning — not an Error. AC-03: Warning rows are included in the issues table but excluded from the Error count. AC-04: Serial Number is fully optional — no flag raised whether absent, empty, or populated. AC-05: Warnings do not block the Export Converted XLSX button. Note: Serial Number demoted from Required to Conditional in v1.2.

label: EP-03 — Status & Compliance
text: Understanding dataset health at a glance.

label: US-07 — See an overall compliance score
text: US-07 — See an overall compliance score EP-03 — Status & Compliance Field Detail Persona Operations Manager Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.1 User Story: As an Operations Manager, I want to see a single compliance score for the dataset, so that I can quickly understand its overall readiness for upload without reviewing every row. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Compliance score is displayed as a percentage. AC-02: Score = clean rows / (total rows − check-internally rows) × 100. AC-03: Check Internally rows are excluded from the denominator. AC-04: Score bar is green ≥80%, amber 50–79%, red <50%. AC-05: Score updates automatically after each Manual Review resolution.

label: US-08 — Distinguish between hard errors and check-internally flags
text: US-08 — Distinguish between hard errors and check-internally flags EP-03 — Status & Compliance Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v1.1 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want empty Asset and Coordinates fields to be flagged differently from hard errors, so that I'm not penalised for information that may already exist in our internal records. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: When Asset field is empty, the row is flagged as "Check Internally" — not as an Error. AC-02: When Coordinates field is empty, the row is flagged as "Check Internally" — not as an Error. AC-03: Check Internally rows are counted in a dedicated summary card. AC-04: Check Internally rows are excluded from the compliance score denominator. AC-05: The issues table includes a "Check Internally" filter tab. label: EP-04 — Conversion Engine

label: US-10 — Have Element values derived and converted automatically
text: US-10 — Have Element values derived and converted automatically EP-04 — Conversion Engine Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.0 / v2.1 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to automatically build the Input Source Component value from the raw data columns and look up its Platform A and Platform B equivalents, so that I don't have to manually apply conversion formulas. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: If Material column is present and non-empty: Input Source Component = Component + " - " + Material. AC-02: If Material is absent/empty but Element column is present: Input Source Component = Component + " - " + Element. AC-03: If neither suffix column is present/populated: Input Source Component = Component alone. AC-04: Concatenation uses a LEN()=0 guard — not ISBLANK() — to correctly handle empty-string cells. AC-05: If found in conversion table, Platform A Element and Platform B Element are populated from columns B and C. AC-06: If not found, both columns show "MANUAL REVIEW: [original value]" and the row is flagged. Note: Multi-format support (Material vs Element fallback) and ISBLANK→LEN fix added in v2.1.

label: US-11 — Have Anomaly Type values derived and converted automatically
text: US-11 — Have Anomaly Type values derived and converted automatically EP-04 — Conversion Engine Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.0 / v2.1 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to automatically build the Input Source Damage Type value and look up its Platform A and Platform B equivalents, so that damage type conversion happens without any manual steps. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: If Type column is present, it is used as the base value. AC-02: If Type is absent but Anomaly Type column is present, it is used as the base value. AC-03: If Subtype is present and non-empty: Input Source Damage Type = base + " - " + Subtype. AC-04: If Subtype is absent or empty: Input Source Damage Type = base value alone (no trailing " - "). AC-05: Concatenation uses a LEN()=0 guard — not ISBLANK(). AC-06: If found in conversion table, Platform A Anomaly Type and Platform B Anomaly Type are populated. AC-07: If not found, both columns show "MANUAL REVIEW: [original value]". Note: Type vs Anomaly Type column fallback added in v2.1. Fixes the trailing dash bug.

Acceptance Criteria AC-01: "Value 1" maps to Platform A and Platform B equivalents. [Values withheld.] AC-02: "Value 2" maps to Platform A and Platform B equivalents. [Values withheld.] AC-03: "Value 3" maps to Platform A and Platform B equivalents. [Values withheld.] AC-04: "Value 4" maps to Platform A and Platform B equivalents. [Values withheld.] AC-05: Values not found in the Blade Side conversion table are flagged as Manual Review.

label: US-13 — Process datasets from multiple source platform export formats
text: US-13 — Process datasets from multiple source platform export formats EP-04 — Conversion Engine Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.1 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the tool to correctly process datasets from different clients even when the column structure varies, so that I don't have to manually reformat files before uploading. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Format A format (Component + Material columns) is processed correctly. AC-02: Format B format (Component + Element columns) is processed correctly. AC-03: Format A format (Type + Subtype columns) is processed correctly. AC-04: Format B format (Anomaly Type + Subtype columns) is processed correctly. label: US-18 — Export a validation issues report

text: US-19 — Export a converted XLSX working document EP-07 — Export Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want to download a formatted XLSX file with all three nomenclature columns populated, so that I have a working document ready for Platform A upload and Platform B submission. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Exported XLSX contains two tabs: "Damages Report" and "Conversions". AC-02: "Damages Report" tab matches the column order of the approved reference file exactly. AC-03: Derived columns use live VLOOKUP formulas referencing the Conversions tab. AC-04: VLOOKUP formulas use LEN()=0 guards to handle empty-string cells correctly. AC-05: Resolved Manual Review values are written as static values in the output. AC-06: Output filename incorporates source filename and export date. AC-07: Exported file header row is frozen at row 1.

label: US-20 — Have the Conversions tab be editable and extensible
text: US-20 — Have the Conversions tab be editable and extensible EP-07 — Export Field Detail Persona Engineering / Data Lead Priority Should Have Status Done Version v2.0 User Story: As a Engineering / Data Lead, I want the Conversions tab in the exported XLSX to be structured and editable, so that I can add new mapping rows when new damage types or component combinations appear. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Conversions tab contains three clearly labeled sections: Element / Component, Anomaly Type, Blade Side. AC-02: Each section has column headers: Input Source, Platform A, Platform B. AC-03: A note instructs Engineering how to add new rows. AC-04: VLOOKUP formulas reference defined row ranges in the Conversions tab. AC-05: Adding a row within the existing range causes VLOOKUPs to pick it up automatically. AC-06: Known limitation: adding rows beyond the current range requires manual formula range updates.

label: US-26 — Open image links directly from the exported report
text: US-26 — Open image links directly from the exported report EP-07 — Export Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Should Have Status Done Version v2.6–v2.7 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want the image links in the exported report to be clickable, so that I can open a referenced image without copying a URL out of a cell. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Cells in the Links and Source Images columns holding an http or https value carry a real hyperlink. AC-02: The URL remains visible as the cell's display text. AC-03: Source Image Reference is left as plain text, being an identifier rather than a URL. AC-04: The exported URL is byte-for-byte identical to the URL in the source file. AC-05: Where the source cell shows a friendly label but carries a hyperlink, the underlying URL is used rather than the label. Note: AC-04 is the v2.7 fix. Reading a hyperlink returns its XML entities still encoded, and writing it back encodes them a second time; the resulting URL failed signature matching at the storage provider. Entities are now decoded on ingestion. Links are time-limited by the source system, roughly a 30 day window, which the tool does not yet warn about.

label: US-27 — Distinguish the blade from the two serial numbers in the output
text: US-27 — Distinguish the blade from the two serial numbers in the output EP-07 — Export Field Detail Persona Engineering / Data Lead Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.5 User Story: As an Engineering / Data Lead, I want the blade identifier and the two serial numbers to occupy separate output columns, so that the Asset field means one thing and the upload is not carrying a turbine number where a blade letter belongs. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Asset (D) carries the blade letter, A to C, and nothing else. AC-02: Turbine Serial Number (E) carries the value the input supplies in its Asset column. AC-03: Asset Serial Number (F) carries the value the input supplies as a serial number. AC-04: The blade letter resolves from a dedicated Blade column, a Blade Position column, a full label such as "Blade A: (No Serial Number)", or a bare letter. AC-05: Blade no longer exists as a separate output column; Asset represents it. Note: Before v2.5 the output Asset column carried turbine numbers rather than blade letters. The v2.5 insertion shifted every column after D by one position, which is the root of the width misalignment later fixed at v3.1.1.

label: EP-08 — Output Fidelity
text: Four stories covering defects where the tool produced output that looked correct and was not. Each was found after v2.1 and fixed between v2.7.1 and v3.1.4.

label: US-21 — Read output headers that spell both company names correctly
text: US-21 — Read output headers that spell both company names correctly EP-08 — Output Fidelity Field Detail Persona Engineering / Data Lead Priority Must Have Status Done Version v2.7.1 User Story: As an Engineering / Data Lead, I want the derived output column headers to render both company names as those companies write them, so that a downstream consumer matching on header text does not have to match two spellings of the same name. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: All four previously misrendered headers (columns P, Q, U, Y) render their company name correctly. AC-02: The four headers that were already correct (R, V, W, Z) are unchanged. AC-03: Output column count and order are identical to the previous release. AC-04: The export formulas still resolve to the correct column letters, since the corrected strings are also the keys the formula builder reads. AC-05: Files exported before this release still ingest unchanged; no input alias was added or removed. AC-06: Verification reads the header row from the raw exported file, not from a summary or a description of it. Note: The misrendered strings were a single namespace inside the tool — output header, row key, conversion-field label, Manual Review dropdown key and formula lookup key at once. Correcting only the header text would have broken the formulas. LIM-07 is closed by this story.

label: US-22 — Have dates arrive intact regardless of my timezone
text: US-22 — Have dates arrive intact regardless of my timezone EP-08 — Output Fidelity Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v3.0 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want an inspection date to reach the export as the date the file actually contains, so that I am neither shipping the wrong day nor clearing a validation error on every dated row. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: A date read from a CSV produces the same calendar date in every timezone. AC-02: A date read from an XLSX date cell produces the same calendar date in every timezone. AC-03: An ingested date is normalised to YYYY-MM-DD, so it satisfies the date rule the validator applies to it. AC-04: No row raises a date-format error solely because of how the date was parsed. AC-05: A cell carrying a real time of day retains it rather than being truncated to a bare date. AC-06: Verified across seven timezones spanning UTC-10 to UTC+14, against both CSV and XLSX inputs. Note: Two faults with one cause: the ingestion path preferred the parser's display formatting over the underlying value. The timezone shift affected CSV inputs only; the format fault affected both input kinds everywhere, including UTC.

label: US-23 — Have every column I supply reach the export
text: US-23 — Have every column I supply reach the export EP-08 — Output Fidelity Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Must Have Status Done Version v3.1 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want a column I supplied to carry its values into the export, so that a blank column means the data was absent rather than lost. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: Blade Chamber carries its values into the export when the input supplies them. AC-02: Chord (%) carries its values into the export when the input supplies them. AC-03: Chord (%) is written as a number, consistent with the other numeric measurement columns. AC-04: Output header text is unchanged, so anything downstream matching on it is unaffected. AC-05: Every other output column is unaffected; only the two previously empty columns change. Note: The alias map normalises Blade Chamber to BladeChamber and Chord (%) to Chord(%) on ingestion; the export then looked them up by header text, which retains the space, and both lookups missed. All 39 output columns were audited for the same mismatch — these two were the whole set.

label: US-24 — Read the exported report without resizing columns
text: US-24 — Read the exported report without resizing columns EP-08 — Output Fidelity Field Detail Persona Data Coordinator Priority Should Have Status Done Version v3.1.1–v3.1.4 User Story: As a Data Coordinator, I want each column in the exported report to be wide enough for what it holds, so that I can read a delivered file without resizing columns by hand. Acceptance Criteria AC-01: The width list holds exactly one entry per output column. AC-02: Each width applies to the column it was written for, not to its neighbour. AC-03: Every conversion-driven column seats its widest possible value without clipping. AC-04: Columns whose content the tool never sees keep their existing widths rather than being guessed at. AC-05: Cell values and formulas are byte-identical to the previous release; only the width declarations change. Note: The width list had been one entry short since the v2.5 column insertion, so every column from E onward wore its right-hand neighbour's width. Input Source Component carries a deliberate exception to the general width ceiling, because it is the lookup key the Platform A and Platform B formulas read. text: Updated 2026-09-17 from v2.1 to v2.7, then extended 2026-09-18 to v3.1.4. Three kinds of change in the first pass: 1. Output schema. The D/E/F columns were split (v2.5). Asset now carries the blade letter; turbine and asset serial numbers are separate fields. 2. Sanitization. Generic labels were inconsistent across the previous revision (four competing forms, some producing ungrammatical sentences). The whole document now uses one scheme, defined below. 3. Verification flags. Items marked [verify] could not be confirmed from the change log alone and need checking against a current export before this document is treated as authoritative. They are listed together in "Open verification items" at the end. The tool's own version header and its working file advance together: v2.x / v8.x through v2.7.1, v3.x / v9.x since. This document describes v3.1.4 (working file v9.1.4) . The second pass, on 2026-09-18, carried the document from v2.7 to v3.1.4. That range is four defect fixes: the header misrenderings below (v2.7.1); a date fault that shifted CSV dates back a day west of UTC and made every dated row fail its own YYYY-MM-DD check in every timezone (v3.0); two output columns that wrote an empty cell under a correct header because the export looked them up by header text rather than canonical name (v3.1); and the export's column-width list, one entry short since the v2.5 split and so shifting every width from column E onward onto its right-hand neighbour (v3.1.1 through v3.1.4).

section: Generic labels used in this document
label: Generic labels used in this document
text: This is an internal tool operating between three commercial systems. Their names, and the contents of the conversion tables between them, are withheld. The structure is not. Label: Input Source; Means: The inspection platform the raw dataset is exported from. Column A of the Conversions tab. Label: Platform A; Means: The platform the dataset is being loaded into. Column B of the Conversions tab. Label: Platform B; Means: The manufacturer's system the report is ultimately delivered in. Column C of the Conversions tab. Conversion runs Input Source, then Platform A, then Platform B. All three classify the same physical damage differently, which is the problem this tool exists to solve.

label: Overview
text: This data dictionary defines every field the Anomaly Upload Validator processes, from the raw Input Source export columns through to the derived conversion columns in the exported XLSX. It covers field names, source column mappings, data types, classification, validation rules, and conversion output targets.

label: Field Classification Key
text: Classification: Required; Meaning: Must be present and non-empty in every data row. Missing or invalid values raise an Error. Classification: Conditional; Meaning: Optional. No flag raised if absent or empty. Format validated only when populated. Classification: Check Internally; Meaning: Required in principle but may exist in internal records. Empty gives a Check Internally flag, not an Error, and is excluded from the compliance score. Classification: Raw; Meaning: Source columns used only as inputs to derivation formulas. Not directly validated. Classification: Derived; Meaning: Computed by the tool from raw source columns. Written to the output XLSX as lookup formulas.

label: Column Alias Map
text: The tool normalizes the following column name variants before validation. Applied silently at ingestion. Raw Column Name: Date; Normalized To: Inspection Date; Notes: Input Source uses 'Date'; Platform A requires 'Inspection Date' Raw Column Name: Blade Chamber; Normalized To: BladeChamber; Notes: Space removed to match the Platform A column spec Raw Column Name: Chord (%); Normalized To: Chord(%); Notes: Parenthetical formatting normalized Raw Column Name: Turbine Serial Number; Normalized To: Serial Number; Notes: Input Source full label mapped to the Platform A short label. [verify] This alias predates the v2.5 D/E/F split and may now be ambiguous, since two serial-number fields exist. Raw Column Name: Links; Normalized To: Source Images; Notes: Input Source uses 'Links'; Platform A expects 'Source Images' Since v2.3 the alias map is a fallback rather than the primary mechanism. Columns are matched by content as well as by name: see "Column matching" below.

label: Column matching
text: Added v2.3. Input files vary in column order, column names, and sheet structure, so a fixed-layout assumption failed on any file that did not match the canonical structure exactly. The matcher runs two passes. First a header-alias match, priority-ordered so that a more specific alias wins over a general one. Second a data-shape fingerprint, comparing each candidate column's values against the expected shape of the field. Where alias matches are ambiguous, the closer shape match wins. Where shape scores tie, the column with more distinct values wins, which resolves the case of two identically named columns holding different things at different levels of the record. The header row is detected automatically and is not assumed to be row 1: up to 25 rows of metadata preamble above the header are scanned and skipped. A collapsible confirmation panel shows which input column was bound to each canonical field.

label: Field Reference (part 1)
text: All fields listed in the order they appear in the Damages Report output tab. Output column letters confirmed 2026-09-17 against a current export header row. All previously flagged letters are resolved. The layout below is the real one, and it differs from the v2.1 document in more than position: four fields moved, two were removed, and one is new. Output header names were misrendered in four of eight derived columns. FIXED in v2.7.1. Corrected in v2.7.1 (working file v8.9.1) on 2026-09-17 , verified against a live export, and carried forward unchanged since. All four headers now render both company names correctly. Retained as a record of the defect and of what it showed about the "preserved intentionally" note, not as a description of current behaviour. The defect as it stood through v2.7: two separate name errors, neither applied consistently. Col: P; Header through v2.7: Source-system name, lower-cased mid-word; Error: Casing Col: Q; Header through v2.7: Platform A name, two letters transposed; Error: Transposition Col: R; Header through v2.7: Platform B name; Error: Correct Col: U; Header through v2.7: Source-system name, lower-cased mid-word; Error: Casing Col: V; Header through v2.7: Platform A name; Error: Correct Col: W; Header through v2.7: Platform B name; Error: Correct Col: Y; Header through v2.7: Platform A name, two letters transposed; Error: Transposition Col: Z; Header through v2.7: Platform B name; Error: Correct Four of the eight derived columns carried a wrong rendering of a company name. Two different companies, two different kinds of error, and the same name appeared correct in one column and wrong in another. This settled how the typo item should be read. The v2.1 limitation log records the misspelling as preserved intentionally , which implied a downstream consumer matching on that exact string. A deliberately preserved convention would have been consistent. Four of eight, with one name spelled both ways in the same sheet, was accumulated copy error rather than convention. Consequences worth stating plainly: A consumer matching these columns by header string had to match two spellings of one name to catch all three of its columns. Exports produced before v2.7.1 still carry the old headers, so that remains true when reading one of them. Correcting all four was a single normalization, not a schema negotiation.

label: Field Reference (part 2)
text: Nothing depended on a misrendered form. The question for Engineering was not "may I fix the spelling" but "what matched on those strings when they were preserved, and does it still". Answered in the closure below. Only the transposition was ever tracked, as LIM-07. The casing error was never recorded anywhere and was found during this revision. Both were corrected together in v2.7.1. LIM-07: CLOSED, 2026-09-18. Closed by the v2.7.1 correction, verified against the header row of a live export read from the raw file rather than from a summary. It is closed as copy error, not convention . The v2.1 log recorded the misspelling as preserved intentionally , which implied a downstream consumer matching on that exact string. Nothing did. Before the correction the tool was searched for all four misrendered strings: every occurrence was on the output side, and the input-side column matcher — both its alias map and its field signatures — contained neither spelling. No ingestion path depended on a misrendered form, so none was made tolerant of one, and files exported before the change ingest exactly as they did before. The question this document put to Engineering, "what matched on those strings when they were preserved, and does it still", is answered: nothing did, and nothing does. The casing error takes no entry of its own. It was found and fixed within the same change, so it was never an open item. Scope note: the v2.1 limitation log that holds the LIM-07 entry is not part of this sanitized document set. This records the closure; if that log is maintained separately it still shows LIM-07 open and needs the same update. Sanitized note: these headers appear in this document under generic labels, so neither error surfaces here. Both are recorded because they describe every export produced up to v2.7.1, which anyone opening an older file will still see. What changed against the v2.1 document, beyond position Blade is gone as an output column. Asset in column D represents it fully. This closes the open question from the v2.5 entry. Recommendation is gone. It was listed in the v2.1 dictionary and does not appear in the current export. Links and Source Images are both present as separate columns. label: Field Reference (part 3)
text: Propagation Type, OpSeverity and Monitoring Recommendation now sit at I, K and L, between Critical and Damage Location, rather than near the end. Date moved to J. Source Image Expiration Date is new and undocumented. Note on the pass-through fields. Propagation Type, OpSeverity, Monitoring Recommendation and Tasks were defined in this document at v2.1 and were correct. What was wrong was the tool: the matcher held no field signatures for them, so it never bound the input column and the export wrote a header with nothing beneath it. Signatures were added at v2.4. The definitions did not change. Derived Fields Computed by the tool from raw source columns. Written as lookup formulas in the output XLSX. Column references confirmed 2026-09-17. The change log's references to a Material slot at N and a Type slot at R, and this document's previous references to O, T and W, were all pre-v2.5 values. The v2.5 insertion shifted every one of them by exactly one position, which is why the two sets never reconciled. The values below are post-v2.5 and match the current export. Field: Input Source Component; Col: P; Formula: IF(LEN(O2)>0, N2&" - "&O2, N2) Field: Platform A Element; Col: Q; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(P2, Conversions!A:C, 2, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&P2) Field: Platform B Element; Col: R; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(P2, Conversions!A:C, 3, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&P2) Field: Input Source Damage Type; Col: U; Formula: IF(LEN(T2)>0, S2&" - "&T2, S2) Field: Platform A Anomaly Type; Col: V; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(U2, Conversions!A:C, 2, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&U2) Field: Platform B Anomaly Type; Col: W; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(U2, Conversions!A:C, 3, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&U2) Field: Platform A Blade Side; Col: Y; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(X2, Conversions!A:C, 2, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&X2) Field: Platform B Blade Side; Col: Z; Formula: IFERROR(VLOOKUP(X2, Conversions!A:C, 3, FALSE), "MANUAL REVIEW: "&X2) Row 2 shown as the example row. LEN() is used rather than ISBLANK() because ISBLANK() returns FALSE for an empty-string cell, which produced a trailing separator on the derived value. Fixed at v2.1. Derivation rule, added v2.4. Any raw input value the export needs is read from the untouched input row, never from the working row.

label: Field Reference (part 4)

The output Material slot carries the effective suffix, Material for Format A and Element for Format B. The output Type slot carries the damage base, Type for Format A and Anomaly Type for Format B.

label: Conversion Lookup Tables
text: The three lookup tables live in the Conversions tab of the exported XLSX. Columns are A (Input Source) then B (Platform A) then C (Platform B). What is published here and what is not. The structure of the conversion problem is described below. The tables themselves are not, because the category names, code values and the mappings between them are the commercial property of the platforms and the manufacturers involved. The redaction is deliberate and is marked where it applies rather than left as a silent gap. Structure, which is publishable: Three separate taxonomies are in play, and none of them classifies damage the same way. The mapping between them is uneven in both directions: some source categories collapse together downstream, others split apart. Severity is an ordinal scale. Some source categories have no clean target at all. These are held for manual review rather than guessed at, which is why conversion is a decision with exceptions rather than a lookup. Illustrative shape only, with invented values: [input category A] -> [platform A category 2] -> [platform B code X] [input category B] -> [platform A category 2] -> [platform B code X] [input category C] -> (no clean target) -> held for manual review Element / Component Conversions Lookup key: Input Source Component . [Table withheld. See the redaction note above.] Anomaly Type Conversions Lookup key: Input Source Damage Type . [Table withheld. See the redaction note above.] Blade Side Conversions Lookup key: Blade Side , a direct lookup with no concatenation. [Table withheld. See the redaction note above.] Table currency The tool currently uses the original key set. A reconciled union table built from the conversion tables of genuine delivered files is staged but not wired in , pending confirmation of four conflicting mappings where the same source value resolves to different targets in files of different dates. Reconciliation rule. The tables reconcile by union, not intersection. A key absent from one client's table is a key that client's data has never needed. Absent does not mean retired, and pruning on that basis would silently drop valid mappings.

The export button stays disabled until every Manual Review flag is cleared. Compliance Score Formula Score = ROUND( cleanRows / (totalRows - checkInternallyRows) * 100, 0 ) cleanRows counts rows with no issues of any kind. Check Internally rows are excluded from the denominator.

label: Known Limitations
text: Lookup row ranges in the Damages Report are calculated at export time. Rows added beyond those ranges require the formula references to be updated by hand. Only the first sheet of an input XLSX is processed. Cross-field conditional validation is not implemented, for example requiring BladeChamber when Damage Location is Internal. Duplicate anomaly ID detection is not implemented. Manual Review resolutions are held in browser memory only and are not persisted across sessions. Bulk resolution (v2.2) reduced the cost of redoing them but did not remove it. Image links expire. The signed URLs carried in the Source Images column are time-limited by the source system, typically around a 30 day window. After expiry the link resolves to a not-found error. This is an upstream constraint rather than a tool defect, and the tool does not currently warn about it: a file processed outside the window will export links that silently fail when clicked. One client's conversion model is severity-aware, using severity inside the lookup key together with size-threshold rules. The flat three-column lookup cannot represent it, and that client is out of scope for automated conversion until the model question is decided.

It has since been bracketed against the retained working files instead: bulk resolution is present in the build immediately preceding the column-matcher work and absent from the one before that, and those two builds are dated 1 May and 23 May 2026. That places v2.2 inside May on file evidence rather than on position in the sequence. The bracketing is sound in both directions; the residual weakness is that it rests on file modification times, which can record a later re-save. label: v1.0: Core Validator
text: Release Date: May 2026 · Status: Released Background Wind farm asset owners use Input Source to conduct blade inspections. Datasets exported from Input Source as CSV or XLSX must be imported into Platform A before onward submission to Platform B. Prior to this tool, data coordinators manually checked each upload file, a time-consuming, error-prone process with no standardized output. What Was Built A self-contained HTML file deployable via shared Google Drive with no installation required. Accepts CSV and XLSX uploads, parses them client-side, and validates every row and column against Platform A upload specification. Changes Type: Feature; Feature / Fix: File ingestion; Description: Drag-and-drop or browse for CSV / XLSX. Parsed client-side via SheetJS, with no data transmitted externally. section: v2.4: Pass-Through Field Signatures, Sheet Order, Conversion Key
label: v2.4: Pass-Through Field Signatures, Sheet Order, Conversion Key (part 2)
text: Element section polluted by Blade Side rows; Description: Four Blade Side entries were wrongly embedded at the top of the Element conversion array. Removed, with section-range arithmetic recalculating automatically. Decisions Formulas reference the output slots, never the raw input columns. The output Material slot carries the effective suffix, Material for Format A and Element for Format B. The output Type slot carries the damage base, Type for Format A and Anomaly Type for Format B. One formula path therefore serves both input formats. Any raw input value the export needs is read from the untouched input row, never from the working row. Row processing mutates the working row during derivation, so reading a value back from it after processing returns the transformed value. This is the general rule behind bug 5 and it applies to every future export field.

label: v2.7: URL Entity Double-Encoding Fix
text: Release Date: June 2026 · Status: Released Background The hyperlinks shipped in v2.6 opened a browser and then failed. The storage provider returned a not-found error for URLs that were, to the eye, correct. Changes Type: Fix (bug 7); Feature / Fix: Ampersands double-encoded in URLs; Description: When the XLSX library reads a hyperlink from an input file it returns the URL with XML entities still encoded, so an ampersand arrives as & rather than as & . Passing that value back to the same library to write encodes it a second time, producing &amp; in the output file. The signed URLs used for image storage depend on exact character matching of the query-string signature, so any encoding drift invalidates the signature and the storage provider returns not-found. Fixed by decoding XML entities on ingestion, before the value moves downstream. Verification: the output hyperlink is byte-for-byte identical to the input URL. 1355 characters, 6 ampersands, exact match at both ends. Known Issues at Release Image links expire, and the tool does not warn about it. The signed URLs are time-limited by the source system, typically around a 30 day window, after which the storage provider returns the same not-found error this release fixed. That is an upstream constraint rather than a tool defect, and the two failures are indistinguishable to a user clicking a dead link. A file exported and then left unprocessed past the window will produce a report whose links fail silently. An expiry warning at ingest is a candidate for a future release.

label: v2.7.1: Output Header Name Corrections
text: Release Date: September 2026 · Status: Released Background Four of the eight derived output columns carried a wrong rendering of a company name: two lower-cased a name mid-word, two transposed a pair of letters in another. Neither error was applied consistently, and one name appeared correct in one column and wrong in another within the same sheet. The v2.1 limitation log had recorded one of the two as preserved intentionally , which implied something downstream matched on the misrendered string. Changes Type: Fix (bug 9); Feature / Fix: Four derived output headers misrendered; Description: Columns P, Q, U and Y corrected. The strings were a single namespace inside the tool, serving simultaneously as the output header, the row-object key, the conversion-field label, the Manual Review dropdown key and the lookup key for the column letters the export formulas are built from, so the correction had to be applied across all of them at once. Changing the header text alone would have left the formula builder resolving a key that no longer existed and emitting broken lookups. On the "preserved intentionally" note. Before the change the tool was searched for every occurrence of all four strings. All were on the output side. The input-side column matcher — both its alias map and its field signatures — contained neither spelling, so no ingestion path had ever depended on a misrendered form. The intended asymmetry, correct on the way out and tolerant on the way in, turned out to be unnecessary: nothing needed tolerating. Files exported before this release ingest exactly as they did before. Verification: the header row was read from the raw exported file rather than from a summary, because transcription normalises spelling silently, which is how the defect survived an earlier review. All four corrected, the four already-correct headers unchanged, column count and order identical. LIM-07 is closed by this release , as copy error rather than convention. The casing error was never tracked and needed no entry of its own, having been found and fixed in the same change. Known Issues at Release Exports produced before this release still carry the old headers. A consumer matching those files by header string still has to match two spellings of one name to catch all three of its columns.

label: v3.0: Date Handling Correction (part 1)
text: Release Date: September 2026 · Status: Released Background Two faults in one line of the ingestion path, which preferred the library's display-formatted value over the underlying one for every cell. Changes Type: Fix (bug 10); Feature / Fix: Dates from CSV shifted back one day west of UTC; Description: The XLSX library uses opposite conventions for the two input kinds: a date parsed out of CSV text becomes a timestamp at UTC midnight, while a date cell read from a real XLSX becomes one at local midnight. The display value is built with local accessors, so it was correct for the XLSX case and wrong for the CSV one. A 2026-04-12 inspection read from CSV displayed as 4/11/26 anywhere west of UTC. Fixed by stopping the CSV parser coercing text into dates at all, so CSV dates stay the literal strings the file contained. Type: Fix (bug 11); Feature / Fix: Every dated row failed its own date-format check; Description: The display value renders as 4/12/26 in every timezone, which never satisfied the YYYY-MM-DD rule that both the date field signature and its validator test. Every row carrying a date raised a hard error, in every timezone and on both input kinds, and the shape-based fallback for a renamed date column could never match either. Genuine XLSX date cells are now rendered from their components as ISO. Type: Fix; Feature / Fix: Timestamps silently truncated; Description: A cell carrying a real time of day lost it: a 14:30 expiry exported as a bare date. The time is now preserved. A detail worth recording. The serial-to-date conversion carries a sub-minute per-zone skew, because the library builds its epoch from a pre-1900 date and zones then sat on odd historical offsets. In one zone a 2026-04-12 cell lands on 23:59:50 the day before . Reading the components naively would have lost a whole day to ten seconds, so the value is rounded to the nearest minute first. Verification: seven timezones spanning UTC-10 to UTC+14, against both CSV and XLSX inputs, with date-related errors going from four per four-row file to zero in all fourteen combinations. Scope note The original report of this defect over-generalised: it described the shift as affecting all exports. It affects CSV inputs only . Date cells in real XLSX exports were never shifted, because their display value is formatted from the stored serial rather than from a timestamp.

section: v3.1: Two Output Columns Written Empty
label: v3.1: Two Output Columns Written Empty
text: Release Date: September 2026 · Status: Released Background Blade Chamber and Chord (%) appeared in every export with correct headers and no values beneath them, for any dataset that supplied them. Changes Type: Fix (bug 12); Feature / Fix: Two output columns wrote empty cells under correct headers; Description: The alias map deliberately normalises Blade Chamber to BladeChamber and Chord (%) to Chord(%) on ingestion. The export then looked those values up by the output header text , which retains the space, so both lookups missed and both cells were written empty. The values were read correctly, matched correctly, validated correctly, and then not written. Fixed by pointing the export's source key at the canonical field name; the header text itself is unchanged, so anything downstream matching on it is unaffected. Why it went unnoticed. There was no signal of any kind: no error, no warning, no Manual Review flag. Validation reads the value under its canonical name, where it is present and correct, so the field passes. Only the write missed. In the export the result is indistinguishable from a dataset that never supplied the column. This is the failure class already named at v2.4 — an unmapped field loses its values silently — but one link further down the chain: there the field signature was missing, here the signature works and the output lookup key is wrong. Audit. All 39 output columns were checked for the same mismatch. Three other headers are not canonical field names: Date , which has a working bridge, and Action and Rule , which have no input field at all and are intentionally blank. These two were the whole set. Known Issues at Release Exports produced before this release cannot be repaired from the converted copy. The values are not in it. Any file needing those two columns has to be re-run from the original Input Source export.

Changes Type: Fix (bug 13); Feature / Fix: Column widths shifted one position from column E onward; Description: The width list was authored against the pre-v2.5 layout. The v2.5 split of Asset into Asset , Turbine Serial Number and Asset Serial Number inserted a column at position 5 and the list was never realigned, so every column from E onward wore its right-hand neighbour's width and the last column had none. This was not a missing final entry: a single-letter column rendered 28 wide, a two-character one 26, and a short code 40, while a 36-character identifier was squeezed to 10. Fixed by inserting the one missing entry, which realigns everything after it. Type: Fix; Feature / Fix: Two field descriptions misrendered a company name; Description: The same casing error corrected in the output headers at v2.7.1, in two display-only field descriptions. No occurrence of the misrendered form now remains anywhere in the tool. Verification: the two candidate readings were scored against the widest value each column can actually hold. The shipped alignment mis-sized 24 of 39 columns; the shifted reading, 14. Every implausible width resolves under the shift, which is what identified it.

label: Bug Index, v2.2 to v3.1.4 (part 1)
text: Thirteen defects were found and fixed across this range. Seven carry numbers in the internal change log; the rest were recorded without one and are numbered here for completeness. #: 1; Version: v2.3; Defect: Bare-letter blade values not extracted; Root cause class: Pattern too narrow for real input variation #: 2; Version: v2.3; Defect: Duplicate Component column collision; Root cause class: Ambiguous match with no tiebreaker #: 3; Version: v2.3; Defect: Duplicate Type column collision; Root cause class: Ambiguous match with no tiebreaker #: 4; Version: v2.4; Defect: Format B export produced bare row numbers; Root cause class: Formula referenced a column absent in that format #: 5; Version: v2.4; Defect: Derived component doubled; Root cause class: Transformed value read back as though raw #: 6; Version: v2.4; Defect: Element section polluted by Blade Side rows; Root cause class: Lookup array contents misfiled #: 7; Version: v2.7; Defect: Ampersands double-encoded in URLs; Root cause class: Library decodes on read differently than it encodes on write #: 8; Version: v2.6; Defect: Literal "None" leaking into output; Root cause class: Sentinel value not normalized at ingestion #: 9; Version: v2.7.1; Defect: Four derived output headers misrendered; Root cause class: Copy error propagated by duplication, never by a matching consumer #: 10; Version: v3.0; Defect: CSV dates shifted back one day west of UTC; Root cause class: Library formats a UTC-midnight value with local accessors #: 11; Version: v3.0; Defect: Every dated row failed its own date-format check; Root cause class: Display-formatted value used where the underlying value was required #: 12; Version: v3.1; Defect: Two output columns wrote empty cells under correct headers; Root cause class: Export keyed its lookup on header text, not canonical field name #: 13; Version: v3.1.1; Defect: Column widths shifted one position from column E onward; Root cause class: Positional list never realigned after a column was inserted at v2.5 The pattern worth noting across them. Four of the first eight (1, 2, 3, 8) are the same class of failure: the tool assumed input data was more uniform than it is. Two more (4, 5) come from the derivation pipeline transforming a value and then reading it back as though untouched. Only bug 7 originates outside the tool's own logic.

label: Bug Index, v2.2 to v3.1.4 (part 2)
text: Every one of the first eight surfaced through contact with real data rather than through review, which is the argument for validating against genuine delivered files rather than reconstructed examples. The later five sharpen a different point: silence. Bugs 9, 12 and 13 all produced output that looked plausible. A misrendered header, an empty cell under a correct header, and a column sized for its neighbour all render as a normal-looking spreadsheet, and none raises an error. Bug 12 is the starkest — the value is read, matched and validated correctly, and only the write misses, so the export is indistinguishable from a dataset that never supplied the column. Bug 11 is the opposite and was louder than it looked: it raised a hard error on every dated row in every timezone, which is the kind of noise that gets worked around rather than investigated. Three of the five (12, 13, and the shift in 11) trace to a positional or naming assumption left behind when a schema changed underneath it, which is the argument for checking the fixed-layout artefacts — output column lists, width arrays, lookup keys — whenever a column is inserted.

section: Archive note: v3.0 to v3.1.3 working files are reconstructions
label: Archive note: v3.0 to v3.1.3 working files are reconstructions
text: Recorded 2026-09-18. The working files for v3.0, v3.1, v3.1.1, v3.1.2 and v3.1.3 were not retained when those releases were made. Each release was produced by renaming the previous working file rather than copying it, so at any moment only the newest build existed on disk. The gap was noticed when the intermediate builds were called for. They have been reconstructed and archived. The method was to replay each change forward from the retained v2.7.1 working file , in the order the changes were originally made, rather than to unpick them backward from v3.1.4 — a backward reconstruction produces files that cannot be checked against anything. What validates them. Replaying every step lands on a v3.1.4 working file that is byte-for-byte identical to the real one, SHA-256 c37973f8… . Since the endpoint reproduces exactly, each intermediate state on the path to it is also correct. Independently, every reconstructed build was run through the export path and shows exactly the defect profile its release entry describes and no other: v3.0 still writes two columns empty, the width count first reaches one-per-column at v3.1.1, and the Input Source Component width moves 26 → 32 → 45 → 51 across the releases that changed it. Each build differs from its predecessor by that release's change alone. What is not identical. These are faithful reconstructions of the file contents, not the original files. Their filesystem timestamps are the reconstruction date, not the original build dates. Anything relying on file modification time to date a build should treat v3.0 to v3.1.3 as undated and use this document instead. Practice change.
